decisions.original_gate_result: failed on the MSE criterion only

limits: Only 111 drug instances, and a drug mean averages away cell-to-cell variation.
The regrouping question is unanswerable for unseen drugs by construction, which is why an annotation is needed.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.the_question: does pathway membership predict a drug's behaviour?
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.what_i_gated_on: whether a leave-one-out group mean beats the grand mean in mean squared error
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.why_that_is_a_different_question: association and estimation are different. With 21 pathway levels over 111 drug instances, about five drugs per level, a leave-one-out group mean is extremely noisy, so it can fail to beat the baseline even when the grouping carries genuine signal.
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.corrected_verdict: the grouping carries real behavioural signal (permutation p of 0.000 and a correlation of 0.44), but a crude five-drug leave-one-out mean is too noisy to turn that signal into an estimation gain

why_this_is_consistent_with_the_model_le.the_model_uses_shrinkage: ridge pools information across all keys and shrinks the group effects toward the mean, so the same grouping that is too noisy as a raw five-drug average becomes usable inside a regularised fit

the_asymmetry.reading: the library side is worse, which is what one expects if its groups are smaller or its within-group spread is larger; this round does not decompose that and should not speculate further

why_this_is_consistent_with_the_model_le.so_the_prior_story_stands_but_the_estima: the prior is real; exploiting it requires shrinkage
